clue.text: Big group hug encompassing new nostalgia

parts.note: R.E.M. was a big-selling American rock group

indicators.note: the hug wraps around the next piece, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: to hug someone is to embrace them

explanation.surface: A large party embracing in a group hug, overcome with wistful longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big group' reads as a crowd hugging, but it is the rock band R.E.M.; 'encompassing' signals the hug word wrapping around the abbreviation for new.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is fond recollection of the past, the same idea as calling things to memory.

clue.text: Person in favour of titles I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who admires noble titles, confessing to a liking for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb of liking but it rearranges TITLES I.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours rule or privilege by an elite, so is a person in favour of titles and rank.

clue.text: Hard water bubbling to the surface

indicators.note: bubbling water churns, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Mineral-rich water welling up from underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the surface' reads as rising up, but means heading towards the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthward means towards the earth, that is towards the ground's surface.

clue.text: Airline, so spartan

parts.note: BA is British Airways
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: An airline offering no-frills, budget service.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is British Airways, Britain's flag-carrier airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and plain, the same as basic.

clue.text: One feels for a little creature

definitions.text: One feels for a little creature

parts.words: One feels for a little creature
parts.note: not a sympathiser but a feeler belonging to a small animal such as an insect

explanation.surface: A kindly person who sympathises with a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects use their antennae as feelers, so each is one that feels for the creature.

clue.text: Complaining about right hog eating end of mutton

parts.note: CA is circa, about

indicators.note: the hog takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: a hog is a pig

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Grumbling over a greedy pig that is gobbling the last of the lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it might signal a container or reversal, but here it is CA, Latin circa; 'eating' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping means finding fault or grumbling, a synonym for complaining.

clue.text: Class as sin a tenet including murder

indicators.note: the clue words include the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A doctrine that counts killing as a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: To assassinate is to murder, especially a prominent person.

clue.text: Clubs are still incorporating Queen set

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

indicators.note: the still word takes the next piece into its body

parts.note: to lie is to remain still

explanation.surface: Golf clubs that still contain a royal set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' is the card suit, not a society, though a clique is one; 'incorporating' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a close set of people, a small exclusive group.

clue.text: Rise unsteadily clutching worn-out fighter

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece in their grip
moving unsteadily suggests the letters of the word before wobble into a new order

parts.note: something worn-out is old

explanation.surface: Someone tottering to their feet while gripping an exhausted combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like the definition's verb, but it is anagram fodder signalled by 'unsteadily', and 'clutching' wraps that around the worn-out word.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a fighter in an army, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Planet with a revolution following Sun

indicators.note: the piece named first comes after the Sun's letter in the answer

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
a revolution is a complete turn

explanation.surface: A planet completing a full orbit after the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks astronomical in this setting, but it is Sunday's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Ring one chap boxing about to get aggressive

parts.note: to ring is to give a bell, a phone call
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the chap boxes the other piece in, holding it inside

parts.note: a chap is a gent
RE means about, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A man in a boxing ring about to become violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' and 'boxing' paint a prize fight, but the ring is a telephone call and 'boxing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent means hostile and ready to fight, a synonym for aggressive.

clue.text: PM from left remains outside

indicators.note: the remains sit outside, wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
to have left a job is to have quit it

explanation.surface: A prime minister who left office, with relics lying all around.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert ASQUITH was a British Prime Minister (1908-16); 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Asquith led the UK government before and during the early First World War, an example of a prime minister.

clue.text: Do well to shut up!

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
feeling well is feeling fine

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea: behave nicely and stop talking!
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' is not a demand for silence but a verb meaning to imprison.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine someone is to lock them away, which is to shut them up.

clue.text: Bouquet thrown around front of church

indicators.note: the thrown word sits around the next letter

parts.note: something thrown has been sent flying

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bride's flowers tossed in front of the church door after a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' is the bouquet of a wine, its smell, not a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its aroma or perfume, a synonym for scent.

clue.text: Raphael's unfinished painting with modification left

definitions.note: the clue reads 'Raphael is', and the answer names what he is

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its final letter

parts.note: painting in general is art
a modification is a change

explanation.surface: One of Raphael's paintings left incomplete and altered.
explanation.walkthrough: Raphael looks like the Renaissance painter, but here he is the angel of that name; 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is one of the archangels named in scripture, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Actors' single entrance showing discipline

parts.note: the actors of a play form its cast
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Performers making a solo entry that displays their training.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, a verb sense of discipline.

clue.text: Pet returned in end, so treated for worms?

indicators.note: the backward word goes inside the rearranged letters
something treated has been processed or altered, so the letters are rearranged
to return something is to send it back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pet animal is tame

explanation.surface: A pet brought back home in the end, so it could be dosed for worms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges END SO into N...ODES; 'returned' turns TAME into EMAT, which goes 'in' it. The question mark flags that nematodes are only one kind of worm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nematodes are roundworms, an example of worms, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Intimate guys can love inside

parts.note: guys are men

indicators.note: the love letter goes inside the can

parts.note: a can is a tin
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A close friend saying men are able to love inwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' is the verb, to hint, not the adjective meaning close.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate something is to hint at or refer to it, which is to mention it.

clue.text: With end of snout, collar the French delicacy

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled collar
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A pig rooting with its snout for a French gourmet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigs are used to snuffle out this fungus, so the snout fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffles are prized edible fungi, an example of a delicacy.

clue.text: It's tiny, hardly obscuring naked glutes initially

definitions.text: It's tiny, hardly obscuring naked glutes initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A description of a skimpy garment that barely covers the buttocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a skimpy undergarment, and its first letters from 'tiny' to 'glutes' spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a tiny garment that leaves the buttocks almost bare, which the whole clue depicts.

clue.text: Swears around mid-evening after time in bars

indicators.note: the swears piece comes after the time letter in the answer
the swears word goes around the next letter

parts.note: to aver is to swear something is true

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone cursing in the middle of the evening after closing time in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N, the middle letter of 'evening', inside AVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns are pubs, and bars is another word for them.

clue.text: Frock for church?

parts.note: frock read as a verb: to clothe in a clerical frock, to make someone a priest

explanation.surface: A dress suitable for wearing to Sunday service.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to admit someone to holy orders, figuratively putting them into a cleric's frock.

clue.text: Crop circle?

parts.note: read not as a pattern in a field but as a ring left where hair is cropped on a monk's head

explanation.surface: A mysterious flattened pattern in a cornfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved patch on a monk's crown, a circle formed by cropping hair.

clue.text: Gets desires going topless

indicators.note: losing the top letter, the first one of the word

parts.note: yearns means desires

explanation.surface: Someone acquiring their wants by stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain or obtain in return for work, so earns means gets.

clue.text: Popular Star Wars character's after alien attacker

parts.note: something popular is in
Darth Vader is the villain of Star Wars; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A well-loved film villain chasing an extraterrestrial raider.
explanation.walkthrough: Space Invaders were the alien attackers of the classic arcade game; 'after' places the Star Wars villain second.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader is an attacker from outside, as with the aliens of the arcade game.

clue.text: Fuzz catching fellow and robber's heading for nick

indicators.note: the fuzz catches the next piece and holds it inside

parts.note: the fuzz of a carpet or fabric is its pile

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The police nabbing a man and leading a thief off to the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuzz' and 'nick' suggest police and prison, but fuzz is fabric pile and nick means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and to pilfer is to steal small things.

clue.text: Accuse government head surrounded by a right shower

indicators.note: the head letter is enclosed by the shower word

parts.note: a shower is a spell of rain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Charging the head of state, who stands in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: G (government's head) sits inside RAIN, after A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to call them before a court to answer a charge, that is to accuse them formally.

clue.text: Painter's persevering covering spot here and there

indicators.note: the two words cover the answer, which is concealed within their letters

explanation.surface: A dogged artist daubing paint over a blemish in patches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a noun but the definition is the phrase 'spot here and there', a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersperse is to scatter things among others, dotting them here and there.
